paper_title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Recent years have seen rapid progress in 3D shape generation, driven by advances in generative modeling and large-scale 3D datasets. This progress has opened up wide range of applications, from game and film asset creation to AR/VR content authoring and robotic simulation. In many of these settings, the practical goal is to recover high-fidelity 3D mesh from reference images while preserving faithful geometry, fine surface details, and alignment to the observed view. The dominant recipe for this problem is latent diffusion [Rombach et al. 2022]. variational autoencoder (VAE) is first trained to compress 3D shapes into latent space, and diffusion model is then trained to generate within that space. Following this recipe, recent work has largely focused on how to parameterize the VAE latent space. Existing designs can be broadly organized into vecset representations [Zhang et al. 2023, 2024], triplane [Wu et al. 2024], and structured sparse-voxel latents [Li et al. 2026a; Wu et al. 2026; Xiang et al. 2025]. Although these designs encode geometry differently, they share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into learned latent representation and only then modeled by the generator. This latent paradigm carries two limitations for high-fidelity geometry generation. First, VAE reconstruction acts as an information bottleneck: fine details lost during encoding cannot be recovered by the downstream diffusion model. Second, the two-stage pipeline introduces an objective mismatch, because the VAE is optimized for reconstruction whereas the diffusion model is optimized to match the learned latent distribution. The generator is therefore constrained by both the fidelity of the learned representation and the gap between independently trained objectives. ACM Trans. Graph., Vol. 45, No. 6, Article 244. Publication date: December 2026. These observations suggest that further refinement of latent design is unlikely to remove either limitation, and motivate us to revisit the premise of latent compression itself. We therefore take different route and propose Direct3D-V3, latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that operates in the native voxel domain by directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. This places the generator in the same signal space where geometry is ultimately evaluated, but also makes scalability the central challenge: dense SDF volume grows cubically with resolution. To address this, we adopt dualgranularity architecture: patch-level DiT reasons about coarse semantics and global layout on sparse sequence of patch tokens, while lightweight voxel-level DiT restores fine geometric detail at voxel granularity. This coarse-to-fine organization reflects broader principle in high-resolution pixel-space diffusion [Wang et al. 2025; Yu et al. 2025]: global structure and high-frequency detail are easier to model when they are handled at compatible granularities. For 3D geometry, surface sparsity makes this principle particularly effective, since the most informative signed-distance variation lies near the zero-level set. Concretely, the patch-level model operates on surface patches, while the voxel-level model predicts high-frequency details within selected patches. Together, these modules make native SDF diffusion tractable at 15363. Operating directly on SDF voxels introduces new optimization challenge, but also opens up new form of geometric supervision. On the one hand, even small perturbations in predicted SDF values can cause Marching Cubes to extract non-watertight surfaces with open boundaries, failure mode that VAE decoders tend to suppress implicitly by learning the manifold structure of meshes. We address this issue with an implicit manifold regularization loss that penalizes abrupt SDF discontinuities between neighboring voxels, substantially reducing non-watertight artifacts in practice. On the other hand, once the DiT predicts raw SDFs, each grid can be converted directly into mesh via Marching Cubes, allowing rendered normal losses to supervise the SDF voxel output through the extracted mesh. related idea was explored by Hi3DGen [Ye et al. 2025], but its reliance on VAE decoding for normal rendering incurs substantial memory overhead, limiting its applicable resolution to 2563. By contrast, our approach operates without such bottleneck, scaling to resolutions as high as 15363, and the resulting normal supervision yields measurable improvements in both the visual quality and geometric fidelity of the generated meshes. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. With the predicted camera and native SDF voxel output, Direct3DV3 can be extended to generative reconstruction. The camera supplies the input view for test-time refinement, while the raw SDF grid provides geometry that can be optimized without repeatedly passing through heavy VAE decoder. Building on this interface, we first use pre-trained normal prediction model to estimate the normal map of the input image. We then extract mesh from the predicted SDF via Marching Cubes, render the mesh normal map under the predicted camera, and optimize the discrepancy between the rendered normal and the predicted normal. We interleave this normal-based refinement with diffusion sampling, allowing the reconstruction signal to tighten alignment with the input image while the generative prior continues to complete unseen regions and regularize the surface. In summary, the main contributions of this paper are: We propose Direct3D-V3, latent-free DiT framework that trains and samples directly on raw SDF voxel grids in the native voxel domain and scales to resolution of 15363 through dual-granularity architecture. We equip the native voxel formulation with three complementary signals: implicit manifold regularization for SDF consistency, rendered normal supervision for surface detail, and an auxiliary camera branch for alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry. We further show that the latent-free design extends naturally to generative reconstruction, enabling effective normalguided test-time refinement while preserving the geometric prior learned by the generator. Extensive experiments on image-to-3D generation show that Direct3D-V3 achieves competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art latent-based methods, while producing meshes with finer geometric detail and better alignment with the input image.

2 Related Work
2.1 Native 3D Generation
sections.content: Recent progress in 3D generation has been dominated by latent diffusion pipelines, in which variational autoencoder first compresses geometry into compact latent space and diffusion model is then trained to generate in that space [Rombach et al. 2022]. Within this paradigm, one important line of work builds on vecset [Zhang et al. 2023] representations, which provide an implicit latent description of 3D shape through fixed-length set of tokens that can be decoded into neural fields. CLAY [Zhang et al. 2024] scales this representation to controllable large-scale 3D asset generation. TripoSG [Li et al. 2025] further combines vecset latents with large-scale rectified flow training to improve synthesis fidelity. Dora [Chen et al. 2025a] and Hunyuan3D 2.0 [Zhao et al. 2025] study this line from the VAE perspective, showing that sharp edge sampling and stronger crossattention improve the preservation of fine geometric structures during shape autoencoding. Another representative family uses explicit triplane features. Direct3D [Wu et al. 2024] factorizes the latent into three orthogonal feature planes, injecting explicit positional structure into the latent representation and making diffusion modeling easier to scale than purely implicit token sets. Hyper3D [Guo et al. 2025] further augments the triplane latent with low-resolution 3D grid latent, which supplements explicit 3D information and supports higher resolution representation with more efficient training. third and rapidly growing family uses sparse voxel structures as the latent representation. TRELLIS [Xiang et al. 2025] proposes the unified structured latent representation, which can be decoded into multiple downstream 3D formats, including NeRF [Mildenhall et al. 2021], FlexiCubes [Shen et al. 2023], and 3D Gaussian Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain 244:3 Splatting [Kerbl et al. 2023]. Direct3D-S2 [Wu et al. 2026] introduces spatial sparse attention, which significantly improves both training and inference efficiency for high resolution generation. SparseFlex [He et al. 2025b] focuses on high resolution shape modeling with arbitrary topology, extending sparse structured generation to more flexible geometric outputs. Sparc3D [Li et al. 2026a] introduces sparse deformable marching cubes representation that can efficiently convert raw meshes to high resolution watertight ones. TRELLIS2 [Xiang et al. 2026] introduces new sparse voxel structure, O-Voxel, that can jointly encode geometry and appearance in compact native representation. Despite their differences in architecture and engineering, all of these methods still rely on compressing geometry into learned latent space before generation. Our work departs from this common assumption and asks whether the latent stage can be removed entirely.

sections.title: 2.2 Latent-Free Diffusion Models
sections.content: The idea of training diffusion models directly in data space has deep roots in image generation. Early models such as DDPM [Ho et al. 2020], Improved DDPM [Nichol and Dhariwal 2021], ADM [Dhariwal and Nichol 2021], and EDM [Karras et al. 2022] all operate directly in pixel space and establish the effectiveness of end-toend denoising in the original signal domain. As model scale increased, however, many works shifted to latent space for efficiency. LDM [Rombach et al. 2022] made latent compression the dominant recipe for high-resolution diffusion, and transformer-based generators such as DiT [Peebles and Xie 2023] and U-ViT [Bao et al. 2023] further strengthened this trend by showing that large transformer backbones remain highly effective when operating on compact latent tokens. Recent work has returned to the question of whether latent compression is necessary at all. JiT [Li and He 2025] argues that diffusion models should directly predict clean data rather than noise-like quantities, and shows that simple large patch transformers can already become strong pixel-space generators without tokenizers or auxiliary losses. DiP [Chen et al. 2025b] studies how to make pixel-space diffusion practical at higher resolution by combining DiT backbone with lightweight patch detailer head, balancing global structure modeling with local detail synthesis. DeCo [Ma et al. 2025] observes that modeling low-frequency semantics and high-frequency details with single transformer is inefficient, and therefore decouples them using semantic DiT, lightweight pixel decoder, and frequency-aware flow matching objective. PixelDiT [Yu et al. 2025] instead adopts fully transformer-based dual-level design, where patch-level DiT captures global semantics and pixel-level DiT restores texture details directly in pixel space. These methods show that latent-free diffusion can be competitive for image generation, but they cannot be directly transferred to 3D generation, where SDF voxel grids are sparse, memory-intensive, and coupled to mesh extraction. SDF-Diffusion [Shim et al. 2023] provides an early 3D counterpart by avoiding VAE compression, yet its generation is limited to 1283 resolution, which restricts the geometric precision of the resulting shapes. Our Direct3D-V3 extends the latent-free principle to high resolution native 3D generation by operating on surface SDF voxel grids and scaling to resolutions such as 15363. ACM Trans. Graph., Vol. 45, No. 6, Article 244. Publication date: December 2026. 244:4 Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Youtian Lin, Feihu Zhang, Philip Torr, Yao Yao, and Xun Cao Fig. 2. Framework of Direct3D-V3. Rather than compressing geometry into learned latent representation, Direct3D-V3 trains and samples directly on raw SDF voxel grids. During training, we extract the SDF voxel grid and surface patch SDF values from the ground-truth mesh, and add Gaussian noise to the surface patch SDF values to form the DiT input x𝑡 . During inference, the first-stage model is used only to provide the surface patch indices; sampling then starts from Gaussian noise on these sparse patches, and the latent-free DiT predicts the clean SDF values directly in the native voxel domain. The patch-level DiT uses the noisy SDF signal, DINOv2 image tokens, and timestep embedding to reason efficiently over global shape semantics, while lightweight voxel-level DiT refines voxel-level SDF values within each selected patch. In parallel, camera prediction branch combines patch-level features with image tokens to regress normalized intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, encouraging the generated shape to remain spatially aligned with the conditioning image.

sections.title: 2.3 Generative Reconstruction
sections.content: One important line of work uses image diffusion priors to improve image-to-3D reconstruction. Zero-1-to-3 [Liu et al. 2023] learns viewpoint-conditioned novel view synthesis from single image and shows that diffusion prior with explicit relative camera control can already support zero-shot 3D reconstruction. SyncDreamer [Liu et al. 2024] improves this direction with synchronized multi-view diffusion model that generates all target views jointly and correlates them through 3D-aware feature attention, substantially improving cross-view consistency. Wonder3D [Long et al. 2024] predicts both multi-view color images and multi-view normal maps through cross-domain diffusion, then fuses these geometric cues into textured mesh reconstruction. InstantMesh [Xu et al. 2024] combines an off-the-shelf multi-view diffusion model with sparseview large reconstruction model and differentiable iso-surface extraction module, enabling high-quality mesh generation in only few seconds. These methods significantly improve coarse structure recovery, novel view consistency, and surface appearance, but their optimization is still driven primarily by image-space consistency rather than direct alignment of fine geometry with the observed input view. Another related line exploits video diffusion priors for view synthesis and reconstruction. Stable Virtual Camera [Zhou et al. 2025] formulates generative view synthesis as general diffusion model ACM Trans. Graph., Vol. 45, No. 6, Article 244. Publication date: December 2026. conditioned on arbitrary input views and target camera trajectories, producing temporally smooth novel views under large viewpoint changes. GEN3C [Ren et al. 2025] further introduces 3D cache built from depth predicted on seed images or previous frames, and conditions video generation on renderings of this cache under userspecified camera trajectories. This design yields more precise camera control and stronger temporal 3D consistency than prior video diffusion models. These methods offer richer camera-aware priors than single-image diffusion, but their supervision still lives mainly in image or video space and is not directly tied to mesh-level geometric detail. Closest to our setting are methods that place reconstruction constraints inside generation itself. ReconViaGen [Chang et al. 2025] designs global geometry conditions for coarse structure, local perview conditions for fine geometry and texture, and rendering-aware velocity compensation to correct the denoising trajectory toward the input views. CUPID [Huang et al. 2025] uses two-stage flow pipeline: it first predicts an occupancy cube and UV cube to estimate the object-centric camera, then uses pose-aligned conditioner to inject pixel-aligned image features for detailed geometry and appearance. Pixal3D [Li et al. 2026b] generates 3D assets in view-aligned space to better preserve image-to-3D correspondence and input details. Our method follows this direction, but benefits from simpler native interface: the latent-free DiT directly outputs SDF voxel grids rather than an intermediate latent representation. This allows the generated geometry to be converted into mesh by Marching Cubes, rendered under the predicted camera, and directly aligned to normal maps estimated from the input view by pre-trained normal predictor. As result, our framework can push fine geometric detail to match the input image more directly, rather than focusing mainly on overall structure or texture.

sections.title: 3 Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers for 3D Generation
sections.content: Existing latent-based methods compress 3D shapes into an intermediate latent space, introducing an unavoidable fidelity gap between the original geometry and what the diffusion model ultimately learns to generate. To circumvent this fundamental limitation, Direct3D-V3 performs training and sampling directly on raw SDF voxel grids, eliminating the VAE entirely, as detailed in Section 3.1. To balance geometric expressiveness with computational tractability at high resolutions, Direct3D-V3 employs two complementary DiT modules operating at patch and voxel granularity respectively, decoupling coarse shape semantics from fine-grained surface detail, as described in Section 3.2. To ensure the geometric validity of generated shapes, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization that enforces smooth SDF transitions between neighboring voxels, detailed in Section 3.3. Since the model predicts SDF voxel grids directly, we can also extract meshes with Marching Cubes and apply rendered normal supervision in the geometric space, as detailed in Section 3.4. Finally, the framework additionally predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image, which pushes the generated mesh to align more closely with the input view, as elaborated in Section 3.5. An overview of the framework is shown in Figure 2.

sections.title: 3.1 Latent-Free Diffusion on SDF Voxel Grids
sections.content: Latent diffusion has become practical way to reduce the cost of high-dimensional generation, but in 3D shape generation the compression stage also constrains the geometry that the diffusion model can learn. 3D VAE must encode detailed surface structures into compact representation and later decode them back to geometry, which can discard fine local detail and introduce the reconstruction bottleneck discussed above. The latent space is also optimized for reconstruction fidelity rather than for the distributional objective used by diffusion, leading to mismatch between the two training stages. We therefore discard the latent space and train the diffusion model directly in the voxel domain, using raw SDF voxel grids as the generative state. Geometric Formulation on SDF Voxel Grids. sections.title: Implicit Manifold Regularization
sections.content: Removing the VAE changes not only the representation space, but also the geometric prior available to the generator. In latent-based Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain 244:7 violate the local distance-field constraint, while leaving valid local variation unconstrained. By injecting this implicit manifold prior directly into the latentfree DiT, the model learns to produce smoother and more coherent TSDF fields, which in turn improves the watertightness of meshes extracted by Marching Cubes. We include this term in the final training objective introduced at the end of the method section.

sections.title: 4 Application: Generative Reconstruction
sections.content: The latent-free DiT can be used not only as generator, but also as native 3D prior for reconstruction. Given single input image, standard image-to-3D generation samples plausible complete shape conditioned on the image, but the generated surface may still deviate from the observed view in fine geometric detail. Our framework exposes two quantities that make test-time reconstruction natural: the DiT predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image, and its clean prediction is the SDF voxel grid itself. We therefore refine the sampling trajectory directly in the SDF domain by comparing normals rendered from the predicted mesh with normals estimated from the input image. This turns the generator into reconstruction prior: the diffusion trajectory maintains plausible unseen geometry, while the visible surface is corrected by an explicit geometric signal from the input view. The generative reconstruction pipeline is illustrated in Figure 5.

In our framework, Marching Cubes and differentiable rendering are applied directly to the DiT output, and gradients can be propagated back to the SDF grid itself. Together, these components form closed reconstruction loop in the native geometry domain.

The normal loss pulls the visible surface toward the input image in the early denoising stage, while the subsequent DiT steps continue to project the sample toward the learned shape distribution. sections.title: 5.4 Generative Reconstruction Results
sections.content: We further evaluate our Direct3D-V3 in the single-view generative reconstruction setting. We compare against TRELLIS [Xiang et al. 2025], TRELLIS2 [Xiang et al. 2026], CUPID [Huang et al. 2025], and ReconViaGen [Chang et al. 2025]. Given single image, Direct3DV3 first samples complete shape from the learned prior, uses the predicted camera parameters to establish the input view, and refines the native SDF prediction with normal-guided test-time optimization. Since the refinement is applied directly to the SDF grid, the observed surface can be corrected in the geometry domain while the diffusion prior continues to regularize unobserved regions. Table 3 reports reconstruction accuracy on GSO using CD, F1score at 0.95 and 0.99, and Volume IoU. Direct3D-V3 achieves the best CD and F1 scores among all compared methods, while obtaining competitive Volume IoU slightly below TRELLIS2. Although these results validate our reconstruction framework on standard benchmark, GSO contains relatively simple scanned objects and does not fully reveal how different methods handle complex geometry. We therefore further compare on AI images and community images, which contain denser local structures, richer visual styles, and more challenging fine detail. As shown in Figure 8, CUPID, ReconViaGen, TRELLIS, and TRELLIS2 recover plausible complete shapes, but their surfaces are often over-smoothed or locally inconsistent with the input image on thin structures, concave parts, and fine details. Direct3D-V3 reconstructs more faithful visible surface geometry, with stronger alignment to the input image, sharper local details, and coherent global completion. We also extend our framework to multi-view inputs with minimal changes. We concatenate the DINOv2 image tokens extracted from all views and inject them into the latent-free DiT through the same cross-attention layers, fine-tuning the model for 20K steps. At inference time, we use the mesh generated by the TRELLIS MultiDiffusion pipeline to obtain the surface patch indices. We evaluate this setting on scenes from the standard Tanks and Temples dataset [Knapitsch et al. 2017]; the qualitative results are shown in Figure 9, where our method reconstructs meshes with sharper and more complete surface details than competing approaches.

sections.title: 6 Conclusion and Limitations
sections.content: We presented Direct3D-V3, latent-free DiT framework that revisits the need for VAE-based compression in high-fidelity 3D generation. Instead of modeling compressed 3D latent representations, Direct3D-V3 performs diffusion in the native voxel domain by directly denoising raw SDF voxel grids. To make this formulation Fig. 11. Qualitative ablation of the camera prediction branch. Adding the branch improves alignment between the generated mesh and the conditioning image, especially for structures visible from the conditioning view. the prediction is optimized entirely in the geometry domain after mesh extraction, further improving surface quality and achieving the best Normal-FID of 68.97. Effect of camera prediction branch. Figure 11 evaluates the auxiliary camera prediction branch. Without this branch, the generated mesh can still be plausible in overall shape, but the geometry visible from the conditioning view may drift from the input image, leading to mismatched local structures. Adding camera prediction provides an explicit alignment signal during training, encouraging the DiT to associate image observations with the corresponding 3D viewpoint. As result, the generated mesh aligns better with the input image while preserving the same overall geometry quality. Effect of patch size. Table 6 reports the generation quality under different patch sizes. Smaller patches assign each token to finer SDF region, which preserves more geometric detail and improves Normal-FID. Second, Direct3D-V3 currently focuses on geometry only. In principle, the latent-free formulation can be extended beyond SDF values by adding channels for texture, material, or PBR attributes to the voxel grid. However, jointly modeling geometry and appearance in this native space will require additional design to keep training stable and to preserve consistency between surface structure and material signals. We leave this unified latent-free geometry and appearance generation setting for future work.
